Live progress for long-running work

Source: R/progress_anim.R
blprog.Rd

Makes a progress bar for a loop or a long computation: the animated bar of bldl(), redrawn in place at no more than 12 frames a second, when the console can redraw a line – a terminal, or the RStudio, Positron, R.app or RKWard console (never a knitr or Jupyter notebook; the options rmoriebricklayer.dynamic or cli.dynamic, or the environment variable R_CLI_DYNAMIC, override the choice). In the RStudio or Positron console the bar is drawn on stdout, elsewhere on stderr. Otherwise a milestone line goes to stderr at each tenth, and nothing is shown when quiet. With total = 0 the work has no count, and the bar is a spinner with the time so far and the current stage (the info text), with a line at each new stage when the console cannot redraw.

Usage

blprog(label, total, quiet = NULL, color = "blue", delay = NULL)

Arguments

label

A short name for the work, shown before the bar.

total

The number of steps, or 0 when the work has no count.

quiet

TRUE, FALSE, or NULL to follow the session (see above).

color

The bar's colour: "blue", "green", "red", "violet" or "amber".

delay

Seconds of work before anything is drawn; NULL takes the package's 0.75.

Value

An object of class rmbl_progress, a list of functions: update(done, info = NULL) sets the steps done (and the text after the bar), tick(by = 1, info = NULL) adds by steps, wait(seconds) sleeps while keeping the animation moving, and done(summary = NULL) ends the bar, clears the line and, when the bar was shown, writes summary on its own line. Each returns the object invisibly.

Details

Progress is shown when a person is watching: an interactive session, or a command line that sets options(morie.progress = TRUE). options(morie.quiet = TRUE) or quiet = TRUE silences it.

Nothing is drawn until the work has run for delay seconds, so a fast call never flashes a bar. A bar made inside a function while a bar made by a calling function is still running stays silent, so nested work shows one bar, for the outer loop.

Updates are cheap: when quiet an update only stores the value, and when drawing, frames are throttled, so $tick() can be called on every iteration of a loop. Call $done() through on.exit(p$done(), add = TRUE) right after making the bar, so the line is cleared and the bar is released even when the work fails or is interrupted:


p <- blprog("bootstrap", B)
on.exit(p$done(), add = TRUE)
for (b in seq_len(B)) {
  ...
  p$tick(info = sprintf("resample 
}

$done() may be called more than once; only the first call acts.

Examples

p <- blprog("squares", 50, delay = 0)
for (i in 1:50) {
  x <- sum(seq_len(i)^2)
  p$tick(info = sprintf("step %d/50", i))
}
p$done("squares: 50 steps")

# work with no count: a spinner and the stage
f <- function() {
  p <- blprog("model", 0, delay = 0)
  on.exit(p$done(), add = TRUE)
  p$update(info = "fitting")
  p$wait(0.2)
  p$update(info = "writing")
  invisible(TRUE)
}
f()
